sections.title: Environmental problems
sections.content:
Key vocabulary for discussing environmental challenges:
• carbon footprint — total greenhouse gases produced by an individual. Flying frequently increases your carbon footprint significantly.
• deforestation — clearing forests on a large scale. Deforestation in the Amazon threatens biodiversity.
• pollution — contamination of the environment. Air pollution in major cities causes serious health problems.
• biodiversity — the variety of life in an ecosystem. Biodiversity loss weakens entire ecosystems.
• drought — a prolonged period without rain. The severe drought destroyed most of the harvest.

sections.title: Solutions and sustainability
sections.content:
Vocabulary for environmental solutions:
• renewable energy — energy from sources that don't run out. Solar and wind are the most popular forms of renewable energy.
• sustainable — able to continue without damaging the environment. Sustainable farming practices protect the soil.
• conservation — protection of natural resources. Wildlife conservation efforts have saved many species.
• carbon neutral — having a net zero carbon footprint. The company aims to be carbon neutral by 2030.
• ecosystem — a community of living organisms interacting with their environment. Coral reefs are one of the richest ecosystems on Earth.

sections.title: Climate change
sections.content:
Words specifically related to climate change:
• greenhouse effect — warming caused by gases trapping heat. The greenhouse effect is intensifying due to human activity.
• emissions — gases released into the atmosphere. Countries are trying to reduce carbon emissions.
• glacier — a large body of ice that moves slowly. Glaciers are melting at an alarming rate.
• fossil fuels — coal, oil, and gas formed from ancient organisms. Burning fossil fuels is the main cause of global warming.

exercises.question: The total amount of greenhouse gases produced by a person's activities is their:
exercises.explanation: Your carbon footprint is the amount of carbon dioxide released due to your activities.

exercises.question: Energy from sources like the sun and wind that won't run out is:
exercises.explanation: Renewable energy comes from natural sources that are constantly replenished.

exercises.question: The variety of different species in a particular habitat is:
exercises.hint: The more species, the richer this is.
exercises.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of plant and animal life in a particular habitat.

exercises.question: The large-scale cutting down of forests is called:
exercises.hint: Trees are removed on a massive scale.
exercises.explanation: Deforestation is the clearing of a wide area of trees.

exercises.question: Coal, oil, and natural gas are known collectively as:
exercises.hint: They were formed millions of years ago.
exercises.explanation: Fossil fuels are natural fuels formed in the geological past from the remains of living organisms.

exercises.question: Having a net zero carbon output is being:
exercises.explanation: Carbon neutral means making no net release of carbon dioxide to the atmosphere.

exercises.question: A long period without rainfall that damages crops is a:
exercises.explanation: A drought is a prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall leading to a shortage of water.

exercises.question: The protection and preservation of natural habitats is:
exercises.hint: Keeping nature safe for the future.
exercises.explanation: Conservation is the protection of plants, animals, and natural areas.
